draft.title: Assumptions and qualitative characteristics
card: Accounting entity
the business is treated as separate from its owner. Only the business's transactions are recorded, not the owner's private ones.
Going concern
the business is assumed to keep operating into the future. It is not assumed to be closing down soon.
Relevance
information is relevant if it can help users make decisions, such as whether to lend money to the business.
Faithful representation
the records show what really happened, completely and without bias, so users can trust them.
draft.remember: Record only the business's own affairs, and make the information useful and true.

a.q: Which action follows the accounting entity assumption?
opts: Keeping the owner's family holiday out of the business records
Recording the business as if it will close next month
Recording only transactions that a bank might ask about
Changing figures so the business looks more profitable
a.why: The business is separate from its owner, so private spending such as a family holiday is not recorded in the business's records. Recording only what a bank might ask about would break the idea of recording completely.
a.clue: Whose affairs belong in the business's records?

b.q: Jas owns a cleaning business in Ballarat. She pays her home electricity bill from the business bank account. How should the business records treat this?
opts: Not as a business expense, because it is a private cost
As a business expense, because the business paid it
As a business expense, because Jas owns the business
As a business expense, if the amount is small
b.why: The entity assumption separates Jas from her business, so her home electricity is a private cost and is not a business expense. Paying it from the business account does not change whose cost it is.
b.clue: Who does the electricity bill belong to, the business or Jas?
